metadata.title: Three You Can Take Back. One You Can't.
metadata.topic: CLAUDE BASICS · WHERE YOUR DATA GOES
metadata.purpose: The four places a detail you type into an AI can go — the conversation, product memory, provider systems, training — staged as a descent, and ranked by the axis the source material never draws: reversibility. Three of the four you can walk back out of. The fourth is a one-way arch.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro am_onyx) — master clock; every beat conforms to measured audio
sources: Inspired by Anthropic's education video 'What does AI know about you?' (Zoe, Anthropic education team). The four-use taxonomy is theirs and is credited on the SOURCES card. Nothing is quoted, screenshotted, or parroted — see SOURCES.md for the three vendor-specific claims stripped under DOUBLE-CHECK LAW.
Visual grammar per VISUAL-GRAMMAR.md — a Dante-structured descent, never named on screen or in narration.
new_components: ClaudeDescent — the four-level tapering descent with passed-level rail. Built once, driven entirely by props. See VISUAL-GRAMMAR.md for the full spec.
ClaudeMemoryReread — the level-2 mechanism: a blank chat, then an account-level card read into it before the user types.
